summary: Ezekiel 15 (8 verses) continues the story of glory. Starting with 'Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,', it moves through themes of glory, idolatry and calls readers toward new heart.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows glory lived out in chebar canal, babylon. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,
Behold, when it was whole, it was suitable for no work. How much less, when the fire has devoured it, and it has been burned, will it yet be suitable for any work?”
I will make the land desolate, because they have acted unfaithfully,” says the Lord Yahweh.

questions.question: What is happening in Ezekiel 15?
questions.answer: In 8 verses, this chapter ezekiel 15 (8 verses) continues the story of glory. starting with 'yahweh’s word came to me, saying,', it moves through themes of glory, idolatry and calls readers toward new heart. The setting is chebar canal, babylon, written to exiles in babylon. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Ezekiel and why 15 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally ezekiel, addressed to exiles in babylon around ~593-571 bc. This chapter fits the book's purpose as visions, oracles — its themes of glory, idolatry build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'faith' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Trust, loyalty to God. In this chapter, it appears in context of glory. For a first-time reader: think of it as trust, loyalty to god, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through glory and idolatry, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 7 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'I will set my face against them. They will go out from the fire, but the fire will still devour them. Then you will know that I am Yahweh, when I set my face against them....' In plain terms: it is making a key point about glory. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
